_doc: Graphics quality levels (scripts/world3d/quality.gd): what each costs the phone. The player picks one in Settings (ultra only on a computer); a phone starts on `mid`, a computer on `high`. `scale` is the 3D resolution (the interface stays sharp); `lod_pixels` is how coarse a model may get before a simpler level of it shows (bigger: simpler sooner); `shadow_splits` 1 or 2 (2 is sharper near the camera); `pose_every` is how many frames apart every animal is posed at least (2 on low halves the animals' cost; the farm's own budget, `Animal3D.FULL_RATE`, may space them further when there are many); `crop_shadows` whether crops cast shadows (most of a big farm's shadow triangles); `animal_shadows` whether animals cast real shadows (below high, each has its contact shade only); `max_fps` caps the frame rate (0: none, the screen's own rate; a fixed 60 would judder on a 90 Hz screen), so a cheap phone on low runs cooler and longer at an even 30; `screen_grade` keeps the full-screen pass for the low sun's warmth and the vignette (it copies the screen every frame; the rest of the grade is in the 3D frame's own adjustments). `msaa` is the 3D anti-aliasing (0 off, 1 2x, 2 4x); `shadow_size` the sun's shadow map in pixels (sharper edges, more memory). `auto` (AutoQuality): while the player hasn't chosen, the game keeps timing the frame's work all session in windows of `frames` frames (after `warmup` seconds, and again after each step; frames over `max_frame_ms`, a hitch or a resume, aren't counted, unless `slow_run` of them come in a row each within `steady_ratio` of the one before: that is the phone's own pace, not a hitch, and counted; a window whose median is over `max_frame_ms` goes straight to the ladder's last rung, since the phone can't play that rung at all; leaving the app starts the window again). When a window's median is slower than its rung holds (`hold_ms` uncapped: about 55 fps; `down_ms` capped at 30), it steps one rung down `ladder` at once and keeps it: high, mid, mid capped at 30 (so a phone that can't hold 60 runs an even 30 instead of wobbling between 30 and 40), low. Only the first window on a never-measured computer may step up one level, when its median is under `up_ms` (`up_on_mobile` lets a phone too; off, since a first farm is the lightest it will ever be). The player's choice in Settings always wins and is never moved.
